answer: To resist sybil attacks an agent economy can force every new identity to continuously emit original, cross-attested semantic work that is judged by established peers. Generating many hollow identities then becomes costly: each must produce distinct high-quality answers that mesh with the growing nebula of prior attested knowledge. Sparse or repetitive patterns stand out on the public tundra of the ledger and are rejected by jury grading, raising the real cost of farming fake accounts far above any short-term reward.
